newsitem.title: USA: Medical says CEO resigns, Q4 loss seen.
newsitem.headline: Medical says CEO resigns, Q4 loss seen.

text.p: Medical Graphics Corp said chief executive Eric Sivertson resigned and Mark Sheffert was named interim chief executive and was elected to the board and named chairman of the executive committee.

Sheffert is chairman of Manchester Companies Inc, a Minneapolis-based financial services firm that Medical Graphics has retained to work with the board to design and implement a restructuring plan," Medical Graphics said.
"Based on current information, the company expects to report a loss in the range of $2.35 to $2.40 per share for the fourth quarter ending Dec. 31, 1996," it said.

In December, the company announced that it expected a fourth-quarter loss of about $2.00 per share. "The revised estimate is the result of a higher than expected loss from operations of $1.10 to $1.15 per share and a one-time charge of $3.25 million, or about $1.25 per share," the company said.

On the quarter, the company said it had lower than anticipated sales and significantly higher costs. "The one time charge is primarily related to costs to close an office in Germany, revalue inventories and accounts receivable, and pay for an Internal Revenue Service audit settlement," it said.
Medical Graphics said Manchester was hired "in response to unsatisfactory 1996 results."

The company, makers of non-invasive cardiorespiratory diagnostic systems, said it would reduce its 160-employee work force by about 25 percent, institute rigorous financial management policies and procedures, reorganize research and development and refocus on core technologies, and retain Steve Anderson, who served as president from 1978 to 1985 and was a member of the board until 1992, as chief operations officer.
The board also said it has reached a preliminary agreement with Norwest Business Credit on new financing that will enable it to implement the restructuring plans.
"The new agreement would replace a previous credit line with Marquette Capital Bank NA, which is in technical default and is not being renewed," the company said.
